locator.text: Equation (5.38), p. 59, in the proof of Lemma 5.4

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Two encodings, neither one the printed formula verbatim. (i) In the generic pipeline that carries Lemma 5.4 (GenericRealizationBounds.stage_growth), the logarithm is already absorbed: the conclusion is a JetRate, ∃C ≥ 0 with ‖D^m U^{[J]}‖ ≤ C q^{-K_m}, K_m = max (L m + 1) (Lbase m) — the paper's K_m ≥ 0 independent of J (the `+1` is precisely the log absorption performed by jetRate_of_log_bound, line 47). The constant is existentially quantified after J and m, so it is the paper's C_{J,m}. The rewriting both ways: Λ_log(q)^{P_{J,m}} q ≤ C_{P} on (0,1], so the paper's display gives the Lean rate with exponent -(K_m+1); conversely the Lean rate is the P = 0 case. (ii) The literal log form, with the Λ_log(q)^{P} factor retained and an exponent independent of the prefix length, is stated by WholeDomainStageBounds.prefix_log_bound, but for the physical sublevel of `physicalQ` rather than for the generic domain Ω of Lemma 5.4. Scope: the JetRate in (i) is along the filter `scaleApproach U q = comap q 𝓝[>]0 ⊓ 𝓟 U`, which by uniform_bound_of_rate (GenericRealization.lean:38) means a bound on U ∩ {0 < q < δ} for some δ > 0, not on all of Ω as the paper states it; this is the form the paper's own proof then uses ("After shrinking the q-neighborhood … the constants and logarithms in (5.38) are absorbed by q^{-1}").
